dashboard_description: Describe a change once and get pull requests across your repositories.
getting_started_description: Three steps from an idea to pull requests.
step_add_repo_body: Add one by URL (GitHub, GitLab or any git host), or pick a local folder in the desktop app.
step_describe_body: Select one or more repositories and say what should change.
step_review_body: Check each diff, then push the branch and open the pull request.
repositories_description: Local git repositories the AI is allowed to work in.
repositories_empty: No repositories yet. Add a local git folder to get started.
new_change_empty: Add a repository first, then come back to describe a change.
runs_description: Progress, diffs and pull requests for each change you started.
runs_empty: No runs yet. Start one from New change.
settings_description: API keys, git provider access and AI model options.
repo_add_description: Choose a folder inside a git repository that has a remote.
repo_unavailable: Folder missing or no longer a git repository
repo_remove_body: The app will forget this repository. The folder and its files are not touched.
error_not_a_git_repository: That folder isn't inside a git repository.
error_no_remote: The repository has no remote, so pull requests can't be opened.
error_repository_not_found: That repository is no longer saved.
error_generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.
new_change_branch_hint: Leave empty to generate one. Only for a single repository.
task_discard_body: The working copy and the branch {branch} are deleted. Your own checkout is not touched.
task_summary_empty: The summary appears when the agent finishes.
task_diff_truncated: The diff is too large to show in full.
settings_ai_description: The model that makes the changes and how long it may work.
settings_key_description: Saved on this computer. Without a key, the agent uses the Claude login on this machine, if there is one.
settings_openai_key_description: Used by Codex when you pick an OpenAI model. Without a key, Codex uses its own login on this machine (codex login), if there is one.
error_repository_unavailable: A selected repository's folder is missing.
error_invalid_state: That action isn't possible right now.
error_invalid_branch: That branch name is invalid or already exists.
error_agent_failed: The agent stopped with an error.
error_timeout: The agent ran out of time.
error_interrupted: The app closed while this was running.
settings_key_unencrypted: This system has no keychain, so the key is stored unencrypted in the app's data folder, readable only by your user account.
engine_unavailable_title: Needs the desktop app or the server
engine_unavailable_body: This page has no engine to work with. Open it in the desktop app, or run the server (for example with Docker) and open the address it prints.
token_description: This server is protected. Enter the access token it was started with (PATCHWORK_TOKEN).
repo_found_empty: No other git repositories found there.
error_outside_repository_roots: The server can only use repositories inside its repository folder.
error_unauthorized: The server rejected the access token.
publish_description: The changes are committed to {branch}, pushed to {remote}, and a pull request into {base} is opened.
publish_description_no_github: The changes are committed to {branch} and pushed to {remote}. This remote isn't on GitHub, so open the pull request on your git host afterwards.
task_pushed_only: Branch {branch} pushed. Open the pull request on your git host.
settings_github_description: A token that can open pull requests on your repositories (fine-grained, with Pull requests and Contents: read and write).
error_nothing_to_publish: There are no changes to publish.
error_git_identity_missing: git has no name and email for commits.
error_push_failed: The branch could not be pushed.
error_github_token_missing: Add a GitHub token in Settings to open pull requests.
repo_checks_hint: Runs in the working copy after the agent finishes. Leave empty for no checks.
bulk_publish_description: Each selected change gets its own commit, push and pull request. Changes whose checks passed are selected.
followup_placeholder: Also update the README to mention the new option.
followup_fix_checks_instruction: The repository's checks fail. Find the cause and fix it so the checks pass, without weakening or skipping them.
followup_hint: The agent continues in the same working copy; the diff, cost and summary cover the whole change.
publish_description_gitlab: The changes are committed to {branch}, pushed to {remote}, and a merge request into {base} is opened.
templates_empty: No templates yet. Save one from New change.
settings_gitlab_description: A token that can open merge requests on your projects (a personal or project access token with the api scope).
error_gitlab_token_missing: Add a GitLab token in Settings to open merge requests.
repo_url_hint: Nothing is downloaded yet: the app clones it into its own data folder the first time a change runs on it, or when you click Clone now. Private repositories use your GitHub or GitLab sign-in.
repo_github_signin_hint: Sign in with GitHub in Settings to pick from your repositories.
repo_remove_body_managed: The app forgets this repository and deletes its own copy. The repository on GitHub or GitLab is not touched.
settings_github_code_intro: Enter this code on GitHub to finish signing in:
settings_github_waiting: Waiting for you to approve on GitHub…
settings_github_denied: The sign-in was denied on GitHub.
settings_github_expired: The sign-in code expired. Try again.
settings_github_client_id_hint: From the GitHub App you registered for Patchwork (Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps). Public, not a secret.
settings_github_needs_client_id: To sign in with GitHub, first add the client ID of your GitHub App below.
settings_github_token_fallback: Or use a personal access token
error_local_paths_disabled: Local folders are turned off on this server. Add the repository by its URL instead.
error_invalid_url: Enter an https://, ssh:// or git@host:owner/name URL.
error_clone_failed: The repository could not be cloned.
error_github_login_unavailable: Add the GitHub App client ID in Settings to sign in with GitHub.
folder_browse_description: Folders on the machine the app's engine runs on.
folder_browse_truncated: Only the first 500 folders are shown.
error_folder_not_found: That folder doesn't exist or can't be read.
repo_clone_pending_hint: Cloned the first time a change runs on it.
settings_github_stopped: The sign-in stopped waiting (for example because the app restarted). Click Sign in with GitHub to get a new code.
settings_section_ai_description: The model that makes the changes, how long it may work, and how it signs in to Anthropic.
settings_section_git_description: How Patchwork reaches GitHub and GitLab: listing and cloning repositories, and opening pull requests.
settings_section_templates_description: Instructions you reuse in the Agent.
settings_github_card_description: Sign in so Patchwork can list your repositories, clone private ones and open pull requests as you.
settings_github_pat_description: Instead of signing in: a fine-grained token with Contents and Pull requests (read and write). Used when you're not signed in.
settings_model_custom_hint: Any model ID the Claude Agent SDK accepts. Other providers need their own agent and aren't supported yet.
agent_enter_hint: Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line.
agent_cannot_reply: Nothing to reply to here: these changes were published or discarded.
agent_start_hint: Pick repositories, then describe what you'd like to change. You can keep talking to the agent after it starts.
agent_repos_hint: Each gets its own branch and working copy.
error_invalid_pull_request: That pull request couldn't be found.
error_unreadable_result: The agent's answer couldn't be read. Try again.
review_no_hosted_repos: None of your repositories are on GitHub or GitLab. Paste a link instead.
explore_repos_hint: The agent looks through these to suggest approaches.
settings_section_reviews_description: What pull request reviews rate by default. You can still change them for each review.
agent_placeholder_review: Paste a pull request link, or pick one under Pull request. Add anything to focus on…
agent_placeholder_explore: Describe what you want to build…
agent_start_hint_review: The agent reads the changes without touching them and rates what you tick from 1 to 5. Ask follow-up questions afterwards.
agent_start_hint_explore: Pick repositories and describe an idea. You'll get 2–4 approaches with trade-offs and a recommendation, and can build one.
agent_pick_pull: Paste a pull request link, or pick a repository and pull request under Pull request.
agent_pick_attributes: Tick at least one thing to rate.
agent_review_pick_hint: Or paste a link into the message.
agent_mode_auto_hint: Pick the mode from what you write
agent_placeholder_auto: Describe a change, paste a pull request to review, or ask how to build something…
agent_placeholder_ask: Ask a question about the code…
agent_start_hint_ask: Pick repositories and ask anything. The agent reads the code to answer and changes nothing. Keep asking afterwards.
agent_repos_hint_ask: The agent reads these to answer. Nothing is changed.
error_agent_not_signed_in: The agent isn't signed in. Add an Anthropic or OpenAI API key under Settings → AI agent, or sign in to Claude or Codex on this machine.
agent_reply_auto_hint: Let the AI tell whether your reply asks for a change
settings_sandbox_on: {agent}'s shell commands run in a sandbox: they can only write in the working copy, only reach package registries, and can't read tokens or credential files.
settings_sandbox_missing: The agent's shell commands aren't sandboxed. Install {tools} on this machine to turn the sandbox on; until then only the command rules stand in the way of pushes and API calls.
settings_sandbox_blocked: The agent's shell commands aren't sandboxed: this system doesn't let bubblewrap create namespaces. In Docker, use the security_opt in compose.yaml. Until then only the command rules stand in the way of pushes and API calls.
settings_sandbox_unsupported: The agent's shell commands aren't sandboxed: this system doesn't support it. Only the command rules stand in the way of pushes and API calls.
settings_sandbox_codex_blocked: Codex can't start its sandbox on this system: it isn't allowed to create the namespaces it needs (in Docker, use the security_opt in compose.yaml; on Ubuntu, AppArmor may forbid it). Its commands will fail until then.
settings_sandbox_codex_unsupported: Codex isn't installed with the app for this system, so OpenAI models can't run here.
agent_switch_hint: Sending turns this conversation into a change: the agent keeps what was said, gets its own branch and can edit files. Nothing is published until you review it.
